newsitem.title: CHILE: Russian probe apparently fell in Bolivia - Chile.
newsitem.headline: Russian probe apparently fell in Bolivia - Chile.

text.p: A Russian space probe carrying 200 grams of plutonium apparently crashed into Bolivia last month and not into the Pacific Ocean off the Chilean coast as once thought, a Chilean official said Friday.

New information suggested that the satellite, which blasted off from Central Asia on November 16 but fell back to earth the next day, probably fell somewhere in Bolivia near the Chilean border, said deputy Foreign Minister Mariano Fernandez.
"Our service's internal information indicates that the Russian satellite fell in Bolivian territory," Fernandez said.
"We understand that Bolivian military forces and representatives of the Russian Embassy in Bolivia have travelled to the area" where the satellite reportedly fell, Fernandez told reporters.

The probe, bound for Mars, was carrying 200 grams of highly radioactive plutonium in four small cannisters as fuel. The fuel cannisters could become separated and would not necessarily fall in the same place as the rest of the satellite, scientists involved in the project have said.

The Chilean navy originally said the probe fell in the Pacific somewhere between Easter Island and the coast of northern Chile, but they never located any wreckage and doubt persisted as to its exact whereabouts.

Fernandez said Bolivians living in the area reported seeing unusual rays of light about the time when the satellite was supposed to have fallen. Most of the Chilean-Bolivian border area is a barren, sparsely-populated plateau.

Chilean officials sharply criticised Russian space authorities after the incident for not giving them more information to help find the satellite, the defence minister calling Russia ''tremendously unwilling'' to help.
